title: Enfield Property Values, Paved Roads & Taxis
summary:
*   Property values in the Enfield Addition were officially re-rated for 1917 taxation, increasing assessments to reflect the enhanced value from new infrastructure like streets, sidewalks, and utility lines.
*   A contract was approved for paving State or 34th Street with a tarvia and trap rock method, extending from Guadalupe Street towards Camp Mabry.
*   Licenses were granted for several "public service cars," indicating the regulation of early taxi or for-hire transportation services.

SPECIAL MEETING OF THE CITY COUNCIL: Austin, Texas, May 14, 1918.

The Council met with all members present.
The Mayor offered the following resolution: Whereas, it is within the knowledge of this
Council that many of the public improvements such as streets, sidewalks, sewer mains, gas
mains, water mains, electric light and power wires and tarviated roads were built in,
about and through Enfield Addition subsequent to the 1st day of January, 1917, which
public improvements were a chief cause in enhancing the values of the properties of said
Enfield Addition,

The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution: RESOLVED BY THE CITY COUNCIL
OF THE CITY OF AUSTIN, TEXAS: That the Superintendent of Streets and Public Improvements
of the City Forwarding
of Dista. st.
authorized.
of Austin, Texas, be and he is hereby authorized and instructed to contract with the
Finley Method Company to tarviate with trap rock 7/8" in size for covering material and
7/10 gallons of tarvia per square yard as Bitumen, State or 34th Street from where it
intersects Guadalupe Street to the city limits in the direction of Camp Mabry. The price
to be paid for said work is to be 26½¢ per square yard for original treatment and 7½¢ per
square yard for each re-treatment.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas--Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes, and Powell, 5; nays none.
APPROVED, May 14, 1918: A. P. Wooldridge, Mayor.
